root_cause.text: cpuidle_select() unconditionally delegated to the governor even when cpuidle_driver->state_count was 1, allowing the ladder governor to assume a non-polling state at index 1 and return an out-of-bounds idle-state index when only state 0 existed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that with only a single polling state registered, “the ladder governor may incorrectly treat state 1 as the first usable state and pass an out-of-bounds index,” causing a “NULL enter callback” crash, and the patch fixes this by adding `if (drv->state_count <= 1) { *stop_tick = false; return 0; }` in `cpuidle_select()` to bypass the governor.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: cpuidle_select() unconditionally delegated to the governor even when cpuidle_driver->state_count was 1, allowing the ladder governor to assume a non-polling state at index 1 and return an out-of-bounds idle-state index when only state 0 existed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that with only a single polling state registered, “the ladder governor may incorrectly treat state 1 as the first usable state and pass an out-of-bounds index,” causing a “NULL enter callback” crash, and the patch fixes this by adding `if (drv->state_count <= 1) { *stop_tick = false; return 0; }` in `cpuidle_select()` to bypass the governor.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip governor selection when the driver has at most one idle state and default to state 0 with the tick running.
intent_record.what: A new early-return conditional was added at the start of cpuidle_select() to check whether drv->state_count is less than or equal to 1; in that case it sets *stop_tick to false and returns 0, along with an explanatory comment, instead of unconditionally calling cpuidle_curr_governor->select(drv, dev, stop_tick).
intent_record.how: At runtime, systems with zero or one idle state will no longer invoke the cpuidle governor selection callback. They will always choose idle state 0 and keep the tick running, avoiding meaningless governor selection logic and preventing potential incorrect behavior when there is nothing to choose among.

grouping_result.intent: Skip governor selection when the driver has at most one idle state and default to state 0 with the tick running.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by avoiding governor selection when only one idle state exists, preventing the governor from choosing an invalid non-existent state index and instead forcing safe state 0 behavior.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional delegation to the governor is the direct root cause: it bypasses any check for drv->state_count <= 1, allowing a governor such as ladder to select an invalid idle-state index when only state 0 exists.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally delegates idle-state selection to the current governor without first checking whether the driver has only one state. When drv->state_count is 1, a governor like ladder can assume state index 1 exists and return an out-of-bounds idle-state index, matching the described root cause.
